run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T17:17:10Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is caused by HTTP 504s on the proxy's "ingress" spans, each expiring at the proxy's ~15.0s timeout while the upstream frontend span underneath keeps running for ~15.0s. The failing request classes are cart operations (load-generator user_add_to_cart / user_view_cart). The chain leads to otel-demo/cartservice: from 17:17:29 its pod repeatedly logs "Wasn't able to connect to redis", its Redis client spans (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE) stop around 17:16-17:21, and its own CartService/AddItem+GetCart error spans appear; frontend /api/cart and checkout GetCart/PlaceOrder error spans follow from the same calls. The Redis dependency (valkey-cart, VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, endpoint 100.96.2.228:6379) stays Running/Ready with 0 restarts and no OOMKilled mark, but its Redis INFO metrics freeze at 17:16:10 and its main-thread CPU rate reaches 0, i.e. it served no commands while cart could not connect. Its container is capped at cpu 10m / memory 10Mi with RSS at ~93% of that 10Mi limit, and it declares no readiness probe, so 'Ready' does not prove it was serving. Separately, cart's own container saturates its 45m CPU quota (throttling 0.16-0.24 baseline -> 0.99 at 17:29) even though its node has spare CPU, which stretches cart latency past the proxy timeout. The incident self-resolved by ~17:29-17:30 (cart and proxy error rates back to 0) with no pod restart. The exact mechanism by which the Redis connection was lost is not proven by the available signals.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span error rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) rose from 0 at 17:15:10 to 0.178/s at 17:16:10, peaked at about 1.46/s during 17:21-17:26, and was back to 0 at 17:30:10; the alert start 17:17:10 falls inside this rise.

The frontend-proxy error spans are operation "ingress" with status tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR", each lasting ~15,000,000 us; the paired "router frontend egress" spans last the same ~15s and carry error="true" with http.status_code="0".

Over 17:10:10-17:33:16 the increase in error-status spans for frontend-proxy was 959.63 on span_name "ingress" and 0 on span_name "router frontend egress"; the proxy's own egress spans carry no error status code.

The sampled 504 traces are load-generator add-to-cart and view-cart requests; in each the frontend server span (operation POST or GET) lasted ~14.999-15.003s and recorded http.status_code="200", i.e. the proxy's ~15s timeout fired at or before the frontend finished.

Pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 (container cart) handled requests normally up to about 17:17:2x, then logged "Wasn't able to connect to redis" followed by "Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised." repeatedly from 17:17:29 through 17:20:59, continuing to at least 17:23:46.

cart service Redis client span rates (HGET ~4.0-5.1/s, HMSET/EXPIRE ~1.8-2.4/s at 17:05-17:19) collapse to 0 by 17:21-17:22, while span_name "POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem" and "POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart" with STATUS_CODE_ERROR rise from 0 to about 0.07-0.09/s and the non-error (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) rates for the same operations fall to 0.

Error-status span increases over 17:10:10-17:33:16 include cart POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 45.23 and GetCart 38.77, frontend GET /api/cart 31.68, POST /api/cart 46.31, executing api route (pages) /api/cart 79.71, checkout oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 6.75 and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 6.75, and frontend-proxy ingress 959.63.

The cart container (limit cpu 45m) raised its CPU usage from ~0.0095 to ~0.028 cores and its CFS throttling ratio from 0.16-0.24 (baseline) to 0.58 at 17:19, 0.75 at 17:21, 0.83 at 17:23, 0.87 at 17:25-17:27 and 0.99 at 17:29.

Node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, which hosts both cart and valkey-cart, did not run out of CPU: total otel-demo container CPU on it fell from ~0.18 to ~0.13 cores at 17:21 and ~0.035 at 17:29; valkey-cart's own throttling ratio stayed low (0.02-0.09) throughout.

valkey-cart's container declares limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi (requests 2m / 4Mi) with image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine, and its container spec contains no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe; pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and lastState empty, started 16:44:07Z.

Service valkey-cart (port 6379, selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart) resolves to a single endpoint 100.96.2.228:6379 belonging to pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr, and the cart deployment sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379.

Redis INFO metrics for the Redis scraped by the otel-collector redisreceiver (which grow in step with cart traffic up to onset, 1.44 MB -> 1.71 MB) freeze exactly at 17:16:10: used_memory stays 1,710,360 B and memory_peak 1,726,344 B for every later sample, while redis_memory_rss_bytes is 9,744,384 B (about 93% of the 10,485,760 B container limit) and the container working set is ~3.87-4.09 MB; Redis main-thread CPU rate drops to 0 by 17:21.

The episode ended without any restart: cart error-status span rate returned to 0 at 17:30:00 and frontend-proxy error rate to 0 at 17:30:10, while cart and valkey-cart pods still show restartCount 0 with running containers started at 16:44:09Z and 16:44:07Z and no lastState.

Checked and found without failure evidence in this window: product-catalog has no error-status span series in 17:10:10-17:33:16 and its sampled oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct spans returned rpc.grpc.status_code="0" in 96-154 us; frontend-proxy container throttling was only 0.024-0.043 and fell to 0, frontend throttling was 0.21-0.37 before onset and fell to 0.066 during the incident; all five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure False.

A separate cart container existed during the window: pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00 (container cart, ~0.0065 CPU/s until about 17:24) attracted 75 "Stopping container cart" (Killing) events and 30 FailedKillPod warnings whose last occurrences are 17:19:59-17:20:00Z with containerd DeadlineExceeded; the only cart ReplicaSet now present is cart-755465879b (owner Deployment cart) and cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s is not in the cart Service endpoints.

The alert is downstream of cartservice losing its Redis connection to valkey-cart: cart's first connect failures (17:17:29), the disappearance of its Redis client spans (~17:16-17:21) and the freezing of Redis used_memory/peak at 17:16:10 all coincide, after which Redis executed no measurable main-thread CPU work while its only client could not connect.

The most likely mechanism inside valkey-cart is memory-limit pressure: the container's memory limit is 10Mi while Redis RSS is 9,744,384 B (~93% of it), leaving roughly 740 KB of headroom for any additional client buffer or allocation, which can stall or fail new connection handling on a single-threaded server. This is unconfirmed - the cgroup working set is only ~3.9 MB and there is no OOMKilled/restart mark.

cart's own 45m CPU quota is a plausible amplifier of the alert: the cart container is throttled in up to 99% of CFS periods during the incident while its node has spare capacity, which can stretch cart requests past the proxy's 15s timeout and explain why frontend spans sit at exactly ~15s. Its rise coincides with (rather than demonstrably preceding) the Redis connect failures, so precedence is unresolved.

An equally open alternative is a client-side failure on the cart pod (Redis connection pool/abortConnect behaviour, connection churn while CPU-throttled) rather than a fault inside valkey-cart; the available signals cannot separate the two.

valkey-cart did not crash or get evicted: the pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, container lastState is empty (no OOMKilled), and its INFO-based redis_memory_* series keep returning stable samples through ~17:23-17:24, so a Redis process death is not supported.

frontend-proxy is not the origin of its own errors: every error span is a 504 that expired at the proxy's ~15s timeout while the upstream frontend span underneath continued to ~15s and returned 200, its egress spans carry 0 error-status spans, and its container throttling fell (0.043 to 0) during the incident.

Rejected: that node-level CPU contention on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae caused the slowdown - total otel-demo container CPU on that node declined during the incident and all nodes report no Memory/Disk/PID pressure; only cart's per-container quota was saturated.

Rejected as this cause: the repeated kill/FailedKillPod loop on pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s was considered but it is not in the cart Service endpoints, is not owned by the only (current) cart ReplicaSet cart-755465879b, sits on a different node, and its last event timestamp (17:19:59-17:20:00) is after the 17:16-17:17 onset; no evidence ties it to the served traffic.

Verify valkey-cart serving behaviour directly (redis-cli PING/INFO from the cart pod's network context, and the valkey container's own state on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae), and raise its memory limit above 10Mi plus add a readiness probe (e.g. redis-cli ping) so that Ready reflects Redis actually serving.

Review the cartservice Redis client configuration (StackExchange.Redis connectTimeout/abortConnect/connection pool) and consider raising the cart container CPU limit from 45m, since it spent up to 99% of CFS periods throttled during the incident.

gaps: valkey-cart container logs returned no lines in the window (view e0b7a7d0-c19e-42e7-b241-8c5180a4fafd-t1:2f3640a9-8b18-495e-825e-cf714d0dcc31 status no_data), so whether Redis refused connections (e.g. maxclients) or was blocked internally could not be verified.

No Redis connection/health series are available in this Prometheus (no connected_clients, rejected_connections, maxmemory or OOM signals); kube_* metric series returned no data (view 6a05cdcb-3b71-4fa6-80e3-c10321e22be2-t1:0cc68cec-9ab5-4dec-81b5-09002818abf9 no_data) and the kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready query returned no data (view 5093ceb2-d3c0-49e2-86ad-a027aeea02ee-t1:ba489f2f-148a-4d62-a6c0-3f50057c4baa), so valkey-cart readiness/restart history and connection counts are unknown rather than zero.

The cpu-throttling query filtered on pod names returned no data (view d16737d7-d234-4512-b7c0-921162fbdb92-t1:1a15dd1a-afe4-4697-9c8f-b21cb746af07), so throttling was only measurable through the container-label form actually returned.
cart container logs are only available through 17:23:46 (log read-through limit), so the exact moment cart's Redis connection recovered is unknown; cart's error span rate is the only recovery signal.
The trigger that broke the cart-to-valkey Redis connection at ~17:16 could not be identified; there is no change_history integration, so no record of config, limit or image changes around that time.

NetworkPolicy listing returned no data (view 74ebe2ae-0680-4a5f-92d4-8d362a463a9b-t1:a497886c-e022-46cb-9f86-3124fb0eb38f), so whether a policy blocks cart-to-valkey traffic is unknown; no evidence of a network-path fault was obtained either way.

A Redis-instant query at 17:32 returned no data (view ffbbd4b1-0738-4962-b947-221bf8cc1ea7-t1:eb89246d-3f61-4e49-b7ee-12ef84d367e3), and a filtered log read for cart after 17:26 returned no data (view ffbbd4b1-0738-4962-b947-221bf8cc1ea7-t2:e2457502-a979-4197-9695-0b5e522eb9ed), so post-17:26 cart/Redis state is unobserved rather than healthy.
Unexplained and not tied to this incident: error-status spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (about 1.02 each) for services ad, fraud-detection and recommendation over 17:10:10-17:33:16.
The stuck pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s (FailedKillPod / containerd DeadlineExceeded) has an unknown lifecycle and origin; its container runtime state on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00 was not readable.
next_steps: Exec into the cart pod (or a debug pod on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae) and run redis-cli -h valkey-cart PING and INFO to test whether Redis accepts new connections now and during a replay of the fault.
Inspect the valkey-cart container's cgroup counters on the node (memory.events oom/oom_kill/high, memory.current) and its valkey log destination, since stdout logs are empty.
Capture a full set of Redis server metrics (connected_clients, rejected_connections, maxmemory, blocked_clients) and add a readiness probe so serving state is observable.
Review cartservice StackExchange.Redis settings and the 45m CPU limit on the cart deployment together with the 10Mi memory limit on valkey-cart.
Follow up the FailedKillPod/DeadlineExceeded condition on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00 (containerd/kubelet health) to explain the unkillable cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s container.
